Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Solved instance, one demo request, correct submission.

## Demonstrated rule
The input is a repetitive stripe/template canvas made of a background color and guide stripes (here color 6 in columns 3 and 6, plus some full horizontal guide rows). Sparse anomalies are embedded in the patterned cells (here color 6 where the repeating base pattern would have 5). Transform every guide stripe (entire full horizontal rows and full vertical columns of 6) to color 2. Preserve all other cells exactly, including sparse anomalous 6s outside guide stripes. Do not globally recolor color 6: distinguish full stripe lines from isolated pattern deviations.

Demo: 20x27 input had full horizontal rows 3 and 8 of color 8, and one nearly full vertical line at column 25; output changed those stripe lines to color 2, preserved all other cells (including off-stripe 8s and incidental 7 pattern). Test 28x9 had full horizontal rows at indices 5,6,12,14,18 (1-based) and full vertical stripes at columns 3 and 6; those lines became 2. Off-line anomalies were preserved. Submission was correct.

## Practical procedure
1. Identify all complete horizontal/vertical stripe lines of the guide color, not isolated same-colored cells.
2. Recolor their cells to 2, including intersections.
3. Preserve all remaining cells, dimensions, and values unchanged.
"
}
